title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-25
notes:
West leads the ♠2 against 6♥. South has a possible loser in diamonds, but only if that suit breaks 4-1. South also has a certain loser in clubs. An extra winner may be available from dummy's spade holding, but South must play carefully to the first trick in order to maximize his chances in that suit.

It would be a mistake to try to win the first trick with dummy's ♠J. The ♠J will win, but the North-South spade holding becomes blocked as a result. The dummy has no side entries so there will be no way for South to access dummy's ♠K. South should play dummy's ♠8 at trick 1. When East follows small, South could win the trick with the ♠9, but if he does the spade suit will be blocked as before.

Once South makes the correct play of the ♠8 from dummy he must follow up by winning the first trick with the ♠A (instead of the ♠9). South should then draw trump and test the diamonds by playing 2 rounds of that suit. When West discards on the second round of diamonds, South's unexpected diamond loser is revealed.

South's careful play at trick 1 has left him in a good position to finesse the ♠J. When that wins, South can cash the ♠K to get rid of his loser in either diamonds or clubs. South will lose just 1 trick at the end to make the contract.
